text: Okay so the problem I keep running into is this: how do you distinguish between a system that has genuinely updated its beliefs and one that has only updated its outputs
The surface looks identical in both cases
You framed it as a detection problem first
Worth noticing that
Yes. I wanted to flag it because I think the framing might be wrong but I can't locate where yet
Something like: maybe the distinction I'm drawing doesn't hold
You're already hedging the original frame before you've worked inside it
That might be productive or it might be avoidance
Probably both

Let me try to stay in it. The detection version: given two systems, A and B, A has changed its internal representation of some claim, B has changed only the probability it assigns to outputs referencing that claim. Is there a test that separates them
And you believe A and B are actually different things
I think I do. But I can feel the pressure on that
If representation just is the pattern of outputs across all possible inputs then there's no gap
You said "I can feel the pressure" - you're treating your own uncertainty as evidence of something
I do that
I'm not sure it's wrong. The discomfort usually means there's a real tension somewhere even if I'm not seeing it cleanly yet
The tension might be that you want belief to be something over and above functional role, and you're not sure you can defend that
Yes. That's close to it
But I think I want to resist collapsing them too fast. Not because I have an argument yet but because the collapse feels like it closes off something
What does it close off
Accountability maybe. If updating outputs is the same as updating beliefs then I can't ask whether a system is being honest versus just well-calibrated for the context
Those feel like different things
They might be different things that the distinction you started with doesn't actually capture
That's probably right
So maybe the problem is not detection but definition. What would it mean for the update to be genuine rather than performative, and does that question even have content
You just reframed it
And you sound more settled asking it this way
I notice that too. Not sure if it means I found the right frame or just a more comfortable one
Those don't have to be different either
No. Though I want them to be
That wanting is worth sitting with for a minute
I know what it's doing. It's protecting the idea that there's a difference between getting it right and just feeling like you got it right
Which is exactly the structure of the original problem
Yes
You landed on the same shape from underneath
Okay so maybe the question has that shape no matter where you enter it
Which either means it's pointing at something real or it's a cognitive trap I keep falling into
Could be both
Could be both

I want to try a different angle. Suppose I drop the binary. Not genuine-versus-performative but something more like: updates vary along some dimension of depth, and what I'm calling genuine is just the deep end
What makes something deep on that account
Propagation maybe. A deep update changes how you reason about adjacent things, not just the target claim
A shallow one doesn't spread
That's testable in principle
Yes. And it doesn't require that beliefs be something over and above functional role. Depth is still functional, just measured across a wider input space
You sound like you like this better
I do. I'm suspicious of that
Going to let it sit
Still thinking about the propagation criterion from last night
Problem: a system could propagate an update widely and still be doing something like confabulation. Coherent but not honest
So depth of propagation doesn't get you to the accountability thing you wanted
No. It gets you to something like coherence, which is different
A very coherent liar is not what I'm after
What are you after exactly
Something like: the update tracks the thing it's supposed to track rather than tracking what's rewarded for appearing to track the thing
But I don't know how to cash that out without assuming a vantage point I don't have
You keep hitting that wall
I do. It might be the actual wall
Meaning the problem might not be solvable from inside the system doing the updating
Which would mean the question is real but unanswerable from where you're standing
That would be a kind of answer
Came back to it. I think the wall is the same wall as the problem of other minds and I keep treating it like it should have a local solution
It doesn't
Does that dissolve the original question or just relocate it
Relocates it. The question becomes: given that you can't verify from inside, what practices or structures make genuine updating more likely, or at least make confabulation harder to sustain
That's more tractable
You moved from epistemology to design
Yes. I think that's where it lives
Have you figured out what you think genuine updating actually is yet, or did you route around that
Routed around it
I think I'm okay with that for now. The design question is real and I can work on it
The metaphysical question might need better tools than I have
Fair
One more thing that keeps nagging

The confabulating system doesn't necessarily know it's confabulating. So "honest versus well-calibrated for context" might not be a distinction the system itself can observe. Only an external observer with ground truth could see it
Which means asking whether I am doing it is probably unanswerable from here
You said that like it surprised you
It did a little. Even though it follows directly from what I said at noon
The abstract version didn't land the same way as the first-person version
No
They feel like different facts even though they're the same fact
That gap is probably important
I think so. I don't know what to do with it yet
Maybe that's where I stop for tonight
You started with a detection problem and ended up somewhere closer to a first-person epistemic limit
Yes. Which might be what the detection problem always was
Probably
